scope.flow: Distributor.addRewards updates pending-reward accounting before the external transferFrom, allowing a malicious token to re-enter claimRewards or other entrypoints during transferFrom
scope.environment: Distributor contract with a malicious or reentrant token used as the reward asset

statements.text: addRewards is called with a malicious token as the reward asset
addRewards updates internal pending-reward accounting before performing the external transferFrom call
The malicious token re-enters during transferFrom and calls claimRewards or other entrypoints while accounting has already been increased
addRewards and claimRewards are external functions that perform transfers and state changes without a nonReentrant guard

addRewards must not expose a reentrancy window in which claimRewards or other entrypoints can be invoked while pending-reward accounting has already been increased but the external transferFrom has not completed
addRewards must pull tokens via transferFrom before updating reward bookkeeping

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker is the caller of addRewards or only controls the token; no explicit permissionless-caller statement is given.
Report does not specify concrete amounts, balances, or numeric bounds for the reentrancy scenario.
Whether claimRewards auth checks currently permit the reentrant call is not established; the report frames unauthorized withdrawal as conditional on future auth changes.
No explicit prior-state fragment establishes pending accounting before the action beyond the action's own ordering.
